changes: Added a host-neutral, read-only source_lineage_audit command for learning artifacts, including canonical source key/version/policy hash reporting, duplicate canonical source grouping, missing-lineage diagnostics, command policy/process fact registration, focused smoke coverage, and the execution-plan documentation/NAV entry.
usage: Run: lattice source_lineage_audit --domain=learning --json. The command only observes learning lineage stores and prints non_authoritative, gateEvidence=false diagnostics; it does not create proposals, candidates, outcomes, promotion decisions, active playbooks, runtime blocking policy, or DONE settlement rows.
expectedOutcome: Operators can prove whether learning artifacts are being double-counted or missing structured lineage before building seed promotion. The JSON should expose record counts, missingLineageCount, duplicateGroups, canonicalSourceKey, canonicalSourceKeyVersion, canonicalizationPolicyHash, authority, and gateEvidence.
actualTranscript: Focused CLI transcript passed: source_lineage_audit --domain=learning returned schema proofbound.source-lineage-audit.v1 with 1603 source records, 4 missing-lineage records, 364 duplicate canonical groups, authority non_authoritative, gateEvidence false. Unsupported domain runtime fails clearly. source-lineage-audit-smoke passed 6/6. lattice validate passed all 31 configured commands; DONE-required validation passed packages/main build and root npm test.
outcomeDiff: Expected and actual matched for M1 read-only audit. The audit surfaced real lineage duplication/missing-lineage diagnostics but intentionally did not mutate learning stores or activate playbooks.
limitations: This story completes M1 only. It does not implement seed observe, batch proposal, candidate approval, outcome settlement, automatic promotion, default DONE settlement, runtime consumption enforcement, or semantic dedup as a blocker.
pitfalls: done_prepare still has a 300-second no-output timeout failure mode even after validate reaches all configured commands; main advanced during validation once, requiring a second merge. Delivery and review assurance must remain separately signed and must not be inferred from audit output.
